extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting short stories, covering openings, character development, POV, dialogue, setting, plot, conflict, climax, and resolution to improve narrative impact. Aimed at helping writers structure and revise short fiction effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get Started: Emergency Tips
rubrics_metrics.description: "What does your protagonist want?" Clear goals, morally significant actions, meaningful obstacles, unexpected consequences, telling details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin by identifying the protagonist's desire/goal and build the story around morally significant actions and meaningful obstacles. Use unexpected consequences and telling details to generate interest. This is a quick checklist to kick-start a story idea and ensure stakes and specificity are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a Catchy First Paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with tension; unusual, unexpected, action, or conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with something that immediately creates tension or surprise — an unusual situation, an active moment, or conflict — to hook the reader. Avoid slow exposition; show an intriguing moment or detail that raises questions and promises drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop Your Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Know extensive details readers won't see; convey via appearance, actions, dialogue, internal thoughts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a deep inventory of character traits and backstory that inform behavior, even if most details never appear on the page. Reveal character through concrete means: what they do, how they speak, what they notice. Avoid telling the reader obvious summaries; instead, let specifics imply interior life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a Point of View
rubrics_metrics.description: First (easiest), second (engaging but challenging), third (limited or omniscient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately select POV to shape reader intimacy and information. First person offers immediacy; second can engage but is hard to sustain; third can be limited (close to one character) or omniscient (broader knowledge). Maintain consistent POV and use it to control what the reader knows and feels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write Meaningful Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each speaker gets his/her own paragraph"; show emotions through specifics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format dialogue clearly (new paragraph per speaker) and make speech serve character and plot rather than merely conveying information. Use specific actions, physical details, and subtext to show emotions. Avoid on-the-nose exposition; let what characters do and how they speak imply feelings and relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Setting and Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensory details that matter; integrate with characterization and plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select sensory details that reveal character or advance the plot; avoid gratuitous description. Let setting shape action and mood, and use context to provide contrast or irony. Details should be chosen for their dramatic relevance, reinforcing theme or character decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set Up the Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange events deliberately to reveal dramatic significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure events with intention so each incident reveals character or escalates stakes. Cause-and-effect sequencing, foreshadowing, and well-placed details create dramatic significance. Avoid random or merely episodic scenes; ensure each scene contributes to the story's emotional trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create Conflict and Tension
rubrics_metrics.description: "Only trouble is interesting"; use mystery, progression, causality, surprise, empathy, universality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make trouble central — introduce obstacles and escalation that force choices. Employ mystery to sustain interest, ensure logical progression and causal links between events, and use surprise to renew tension. Aim for empathy and universal themes so readers care about outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build to a Crisis or Climax
rubrics_metrics.description: Turning point where characters recognize something new or make crucial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise stakes steadily toward a decisive moment in which characters confront core conflicts and undergo recognition or change. The climax should be the logical culmination of prior choices and revelations, prompting irreversible action or understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find a Resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Show characters changing or seeing differently; open endings, clear resolutions, parallel images, monologue, dialogue, or symbolic imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude by demonstrating some shift in character perception or situation. Resolutions can be explicit or open but should feel earned and thematically resonant. Techniques include parallel images, reflective monologue, meaningful dialogue, or symbolic details that underscore the story’s emotional outcome.
